newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Date set for ex-KB Lux staff sentence.
newsitem.headline: Date set for ex-KB Lux staff sentence.

text.p: Sentence will be pronounced in the trial of two former employees of Kredietbank (KB) Luxembourg, a unit of Belgium's Almanij holding company, on October 23, legal sources said on Tuesday.
Proceedings began on Monday against the men charged with computer fraud, receiving stolen goods and fraud.

The two were among five employees fired by the bank at the start of 1994 after the allegedly fraudulent actions, in particular illegally transferring 20 million marks ($13.1 million) in funds to accounts in eastern Europe, were detected.
KB Luxembourg says it has recovered around 18.3 million marks.
In court on Tuesday the public prosecutor demanded five-year prison sentences for both.
Lawyers for the two men claimed the court was not competent to rule on the charge of receiving stolen goods since the offence was allegedly committed in Slovakia. They asked for their accquittal.
The three others are not being prosecuted under Luxembourg law because they are residents of neighbouring Belgium, which does not extradite its citizens.
